name: Meclizine
summary: Meclizine, sold under the brand name Bonine, among others, is an antihistamine used to treat motion sickness and dizziness (vertigo). It is taken by mouth. Effects generally begin in an hour and last for up to a day.

pharmacology.text: Meclizine is an antagonist at H1 receptors (Ki = 250 nM). It possesses anticholinergic, central nervous system depressant, and local anesthetic effects. Its antiemetic and antivertigo effects are not fully understood, but its central anticholinergic properties are partially responsible. The drug depresses labyrinth excitability and vestibular stimulation, and it may affect the medullary chemoreceptor trigger zone.

uses.text: Meclizine, sold under the brand name Bonine, among others, is an antihistamine used to treat motion sickness and dizziness (vertigo). Use in pregnancy appears safe, but has not been well studied; use in breastfeeding is of unclear safety. Meclizine was patented in 1951 and came into medical use in 1953.
uses.routes: By mouth, under the tongue, in the cheek

sideEffects.text: Common side effects include sleepiness and dry mouth. Serious side effects may include allergic reactions.
